sections.html:
Alabaster is a southern suburb of Birmingham in Shelby County, about 23 miles from downtown Birmingham and 69 miles north of Montgomery. U.S. 31 and Interstate 65 (exit 238) are the main roads in. The 2020 census counted 33,284 residents, the 16th largest total among Alabama cities, and the 2025 estimate is 34,748. The city is the biggest in Shelby County, and its ZIP codes are 35007 and 35114.

Housing here is tight. Families with children make up 40.5% of households, and homeowner vacancy was just 0.8% in 2020. Sellers with a clean, ordinary house often do well on a listing. The cases that struggle are the ones with old systems, unfinished repairs or a tenant, and those are the sellers this page is written for.

Housing measure, 2020 censusAlabaster
Households11,571
Housing units11,990
Units vacant3.5%
Homeowner vacancy rate0.8%
Rental vacancy rate6.0%

Alabaster City Schools split from the Shelby County system on July 1, 2013 and now runs the public schools inside city limits: Creek View Elementary, Meadow View Elementary, Thompson Intermediate, Thompson Middle and Thompson High. Evangel Christian School is a private option. Shelby County Schools covers areas outside Alabaster, Hoover and Pelham.

Families often pick a street by its school zone. Find out which zone your house belongs to and put it near the top of any description you give a buyer.

Building permits come from the city's Building and Engineering Services department at 1953 Municipal Way, Suite 102. The phone number is (205) 664-6823. Accounts for the online permit system, called LAMA, are set up at alabaster.onlama.com. The city adopted the 2021 International Building Code, and Planning and Zoning and Engineering review projects before permits are issued. A Code Enforcement division checks compliance with local ordinances.

The department posts a Homeowner Guide, an Obtaining Permits guide, a permit handbook and a fee schedule. Before you sell, think back over work done to the house: a new roof, a finished basement, a deck. Ask the department whether permits were pulled and whether any remain open. A buyer or a lender may raise the question, and an open permit is easier to close out before an offer than during one. Details are on the Building and Engineering Services page at cityofalabaster.com.

The city sits mostly in the Cahaba and Opossum valleys, split by Pine Ridge, with Buck Creek and Beaverdam Creek draining toward the Cahaba River. The climate is humid subtropical, with hot summers and mild winters. Lots differ a great deal in slope and drainage from one street to the next.

  • Check creek-side lots for flooding before you list.
  • Look at how water runs off hillside or ridge lots.
  • Expect inspectors to test air conditioning, roofs and attic ventilation, since summers are humid.

The city has discussed expanding what it calls the Main Street Medical Mile along Highway 31, with more medical offices, a future civic center and retail. A 350,000 square foot retail complex, District 31, was announced in 2017 for the corner of U.S. 31 and I-65 and has remained under construction. Big projects cut both ways. Some blocks get more traffic and noise, and others get shops and services within a short drive. If your house is near the corridor, say which of those applies.

Shelby County as a whole is growing fast. Its population rose from 195,085 in 2010 to 223,024 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 238,552. Columbiana is the county seat, and the county probate office there records deeds for Alabaster houses.

Shelby County handles assessment and collection. Alabama bills are due October 1 and go delinquent after December 31. An unpaid parcel is sent to probate court in February, advertised in April and offered at a tax sale in May.

Owner-occupied homes of up to 160 acres can claim a homestead exemption. An owner under 65 may exempt up to $4,000 of assessed value from the state portion and $2,000 from the county portion, and seniors and disabled owners can qualify for much more. File at the county office. A buyer must apply separately after the sale, so the next bill may run higher than yours.

Recording the deed carries a state tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, collected by the Shelby County probate office when it files the deed.

sections.h2: Steps to sell an Alabaster house
sections.html:
The order below works for a listing or a direct sale.

  1. Ask the county for the amount currently owed on property tax.
  2. Request a payoff letter if a mortgage is outstanding.
  3. Check with Building and Engineering Services for open permits.
  4. Gather leases if tenants live in the house, and note the zone for the schools.
  5. Choose a closing agent, who searches title, collects the recording tax and prepares the settlement statement.

Expect the closing agent to want every owner on the deed present or represented. If an owner has died, the paperwork to name someone with authority to sign comes first.

With a traditional listing, an Alabaster house usually goes through photos, showings, an inspection, a lender's appraisal and a round of repair requests. Each step can add days, and any one of them can end the deal. A direct cash purchase removes the appraisal and the showing schedule, and the buyer takes the house with its flaws, so there is no repair list to negotiate. Title work and the recording tax still apply, because the deed must be recorded either way.

What you gain is certainty about the date and the amount. What you give up is the chance that a retail buyer pays more for a house in good shape. For a clean, updated home in a school zone families want, a listing may well net more. For a house with a tenant, a roof at the end of its life or a probate timeline, the cash route often wins. Get an offer, set it beside a local agent's price opinion, and decide with both numbers in front of you.

Whichever way you go, a few documents speed things up: the deed or estate papers, the latest property tax bill, mortgage payoff information, any leases and a note listing repairs and permits. Having them ready shortens the time between a yes and a closing.

Alabaster grew from 30,352 residents in 2010 to 33,284 in 2020. A house with old systems, put-off repairs or a tenant may still call for a different path than a standard listing.

  • Inherited houses that heirs do not want to maintain.
  • Rentals with tenants in place.
  • Houses needing roofs, HVAC or foundation work.
  • Owners relocating who cannot manage a long listing.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Alabaster houses as they stand and responds with a written offer. If you decline, you owe nothing. A cash sale skips repair negotiations and the wait on a buyer's loan, so ask for a closing date that fits your move and have the buyer put it in writing.

faqs.q: What county is Alabaster, AL in?
faqs.a: Alabaster is in Shelby County, Alabama. It is the county's largest city, while the county seat is Columbiana.

faqs.q: What is the population of Alabaster, AL?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 33,284 people, and the 2025 estimate is 34,748.

faqs.q: Does Alabaster have its own school system?
faqs.a: Yes. Alabaster City Schools separated from Shelby County Schools on July 1, 2013, and it operates the public schools in the city.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Alabaster?
faqs.a: From Building and Engineering Services at 1953 Municipal Way, Suite 102, or through the city's online LAMA portal. The office phone is (205) 664-6823.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on an Alabaster house?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31. Shelby County handles assessment and collection.
